name: Question 4
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the second column of the matrix $P?$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 13 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,z=[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -12 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that the Jordan matrix $J$ may be written as a composition of Jordan blocks, as follows:

$$
J={J}_{2}(-1)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(2)
$$

So, we have

- one $2\times 2$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =-1,$ and

- one $1\times 1$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =2.$

Therefore, the columns of $P$ form the following chains: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{2}(-1) & : & {v}_{2}\overset{A+I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A+I\,}{\to }0 &  \\ {J}_{1}(2) & : & {v}_{3}\overset{A-2I\,}{\to }0 & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the second column of $P$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to $\lambda =-1.$ 

Now, computing $A+I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Among the given vectors, only $y$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2,$ since

$$
(A+I)y=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 13 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -12 \\ 8\end{aligned}]=z,
$$

and, therefore,

$$
(A+I)^{2}y=(A+I)z=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -12 \\ 8\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],
$$

and we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 13 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\overset{A+I\,}{\to }[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -12 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\overset{A+I\,}{\to }0.\end{aligned}
$$

The other vectors do not satisfy this condition.

Question 4
?

A=[1−202−303−12],J=[−1100−10002]

Consider the matrices above. Given that A=PJP−1 is a Jordan canonical decomposition of A, which of the following could be the second column of the matrix P?

x=[001],y=[7130],z=[−12−128]

a
x only
b
x and z only
c
y and z only
d
z only
e
y only
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the Jordan matrix J may be written as a composition of Jordan blocks, as follows:

J=J2(−1)⊕J1(2) So, we have

  • one 2×2 Jordan block corresponding to λ=−1, and

  • one 1×1 Jordan block corresponding to λ=2.

Therefore, the columns of P form the following chains:

J2(−1):v2→A+Iv1→A+I0J1(2):v3→A−2I0

As a result, the second column of P is a generalized eigenvector of rank 2 corresponding to λ=−1.

Now, computing A+I, we get

A+I=[1−202−303−12]+[100010001]=[2−202−203−13].

Among the given vectors, only y is a generalized eigenvector of rank 2, since

(A+I)y=[2−202−203−13][7130]=[−12−128]=z, and, therefore, (A+I)2y=(A+I)z=[2−202−203−13][−12−128]=[000],

and we can write

[7130]→A+I[−12−128]→A+I0.

The other vectors do not satisfy this condition.
